minutes.headline: Water commissioners held off on a tank-top antenna mount until a second carrier shows interest; drought rules discussed.
minutes.summary: The commissioners heard a proposal for an antenna mounting structure on the Sunny Hill water tank and chose to hold it until a carrier commits. They also discussed the limits of the newly permitted well, expected drought restrictions and enforcement, and a possible subscription tool for forecasting water rates. Prior minutes and adjournment were moved, but the captions do not give the vote results.

votes.motion: Motion to adjourn, made after the clerk treasurer's items.

budget_items.topic: Antenna mounting structure on water tank
budget_items.what_was_said: The superintendent reported a quote from tower engineering professionals; it could not be voted on because it was not on the agenda.
Current carrier revenue helps maintain the tanks; the renewal is about two years away.
Commissioners questioned total cost with one carrier on it and said engineering often costs more than estimated.
Commissioners wanted a long multi-year lease to justify building the mount.
A quote for engineering at the Chase Road tank was described as extreme, so it waits until the tank is inspected.
Reduced water use during a drought would reduce revenue and affect the budget.
A tool to model debt service, revenue and rates was quoted as an approximate yearly subscription, not a firm figure.
An example town project was delayed with inflation raising its cost.

decisions.decision: The antenna mount proposal will be held and not placed on the agenda unless a carrier shows interest.
Wait until April for DEP guidance, then draft a post, letter or postcard to residents on drought restrictions.
The superintendent will send a letter asking the town manager and the select board to consider applying water restrictions to private wells.
Commissioners may send changes to the clerk treasurer on the draft annual report, which will be assembled probably next week.

what_happened.line: Commissioners held a proposed antenna mount on the Sunny Hill water tank and will not place it on an agenda unless a carrier shows interest.
The superintendent will send a letter asking the town manager and select board to consider applying water restrictions to private wells.
Commissioners plan to wait until April for DEP guidance, then draft a post, letter or postcard to residents on drought restrictions.
The mount could not be voted on because it was not on the agenda; commissioners questioned its total cost and wanted a long multi-year carrier lease first.
Commissioners may send changes on the draft annual report to the clerk treasurer, who will assemble it probably next week.

why_it_matters: Lease payments from the current carrier help maintain the tanks, so whether a second carrier signs affects what water customers' rates must cover.

Drought restrictions would reduce water use and therefore water revenue, and a request to extend restrictions to private wells would reach the town manager and select board, who decide whether they apply to homeowners with wells.
watch_next: April, when DEP drought guidance is expected and a notice to residents on restrictions is to be drafted.
The draft annual report, to be assembled probably the week after this meeting.
